newsitem.title: UK: Latin American insurance sales to double - report.
newsitem.headline: Latin American insurance sales to double - report.

text.p: The market for general insurance in Latin America will double over the next five years, management consultancy Datamonitor said on Monday in its report 'Insurance in Latin America'.
Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Venezuela account for more than 90 percent of insurance premiums in Latin America.
"General insurance premiums in those six countries will nearly double from $20,847 million in 1996 to $38,040 million in 2001, at an average annual growth of 12.8 percent," the report said.
With such rapid growth rates in prospect, foreign insurers are showing interest in these countries.
Foreign companies control a quarter of the Mexican market, where Aegon, Aetna, Allianz and AIG are all present, Datamonitor said.
Mexico is the second largest market in the region after Brazil, which had general insurance premiums of $12.136 billion last year.
Datamonitor noted that per capital general insurance premiums were below $100 in all Latin American countries last year, compared with $1,192 in Germany and $894 in France.
